ODFL.thesis_one_line: The best-run US trucking company, debt-free and just turning a corner, but priced for growth its own capex spending doesn't support yet.
kill_criteria: Revenue/day growth (company-published monthly metric) turns negative again for two consecutive months.
Operating ratio deteriorates >100bps YoY for a full quarter (reversing the Q2 FY26 improvement).
Quarterly capex resumes above a $180M/quarter run-rate without a corresponding reacceleration in revenue growth (confirms the FCF-optical-cheapness thesis breaking).
Net debt/EBITDA (currently net cash) turns >0.3x (loss of the debt-free position that anchors the quality score).
NTM P/E stays >25x while trailing-4-quarter revenue growth is <5% (valuation and fundamentals re-diverging).
key_adverse_facts: TTM capex ($279.3M) is roughly one-third of the FY2023-24 run-rate ($750-770M/yr); this suppresses TTM FCF and makes the stock look cheaper on FCF yield than a normalized capex base would show.
Revenue declined YoY in four of the last five quarters before Q2 FY26's +10.4% print; the inflection is one quarter old.
ODFL gives no formal numeric guidance, so 'raised/cut vs prior range' cannot be assessed the way the addendum asks; only monthly revenue/day commentary exists.
5-year delivered growth is only ~4.1% (v1 data) versus a market-implied growth rate of roughly 20% on a normalized-capex FCF basis.
data_conflicts: My independent reverse DCF on TTM-reported FCF implies ~12-13% embedded growth, materially below V1's 20.1%; reconciled by capex-normalization (Section 7 of dossier) rather than treated as a true conflict.

DV31: ODFL guides 2026 capex to about $380M (10-Q), below its stated historical 10-15% of revenue; the $180M-a-quarter kill threshold is above that range. Debt is about $20M current maturities, not zero.
ODFL.confidence_in_thesis: medium (business quality is high-confidence; the freight-cycle inflection is one-quarter-old evidence, so timing/durability of the turn is lower-confidence)
ODFL.scenario_basis: V1 model, adopted as-is: starting NTM P/E 27.1x normalized-capex FCF base; base case reverts NTM P/E toward the 24.1x peer median as the ~20% embedded growth rate proves unsustainable once capex normalizes off its current suppressed run-rate; no separate dividend layer disclosed in the V1 output.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1's reverse DCF implies ~20% 10-year growth is priced in at a 27.1x NTM P/E; my own DCF on TTM FCF understates this only because TTM capex is temporarily suppressed versus ODFL's historical mid-cycle run-rate, and on a normalized-capex basis the two converge. I agree with V1's 'excessive' read and its negative base-case 3-year return: implied growth (about 16.5% on a $550M capex normalisation and about 14% on the company 2026 capex plan of about $380M, DV31 replication) is above a defensible base case (high-single-digit freight-cycle recovery growth), which is why this is WATCH, not INCLUDE.

PG.thesis_one_line: The world's top household-products company, still growing and still cash-generative, but sales growth has slowed to almost nothing and margins are shrinking.
kill_criteria: Organic sales growth is negative for any full quarter (currently 0%, i.e. one step from this trigger).
Operating margin compression exceeds -200bps YoY for two consecutive quarters (it already has, in FY26 Q2 and Q4).
Core EPS growth guidance for FY2027 is issued below 'in-line to +4%' at the next annual guidance-setting release. [Triggered 2026-07-29: FY2027 core EPS guide is in line to +3% (DV33)]
Long-term debt rises above $26bn without a corresponding accretive acquisition.
FCF/NI conversion falls below 85% for a full fiscal year (currently 94%).
key_adverse_facts: FY2026 organic sales growth was +1% for the full year and flat (0%) in the most recent quarter (Q4 FY26), a real deceleration from the 'in-line to 4%' guided range.
Operating margin compressed YoY in every one of the last four fiscal quarters, worsening to -220bps YoY in FY26 Q4.
Core EPS growth (+1% for FY26) landed at the very bottom of the guided range, and Q4 core EPS specifically fell 3% YoY.
FY2026 capital returned to shareholders ($15.26bn buybacks+dividends) slightly exceeded FCF generated ($15.15bn), leaving no spare cushion.

FY2027 guidance (29 Jul 2026) is below the dossier's own 'in line to +4%' test: organic +1% to +3%, core EPS in line to +3% ($6.89-$7.11), $0.56 per share cost headwind, FCF productivity guided 85-90% (94% in FY2026) [Added 2026-10-08: DV33]
PG.confidence_in_thesis: medium (quality and capital-return durability are high-confidence; near-term growth/margin trajectory is genuinely uncertain given the cost headwind's persistence)
PG.scenario_basis: Starting FY2026 core EPS $6.89 and FCF/share ~$6.52 (94% FCF/NI conversion); base case assumes ~3% aggregate FCF growth plus ~1.5%/yr buyback-driven per-share uplift (~4.5% per-share growth), a flat ~21x core P/E, and a ~3.0% dividend yield; bear assumes growth stalls to 0% and the multiple derates to ~18x; bull assumes organic growth reaccelerates to 4%+ and the multiple re-rates to ~23x. [DV33 2026-10-08: base restated from 7.5% to 6.5% using FY2027 core EPS +1.5% (guide midpoint) then 4.5% per share; bear and bull not re-derived.]

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: PG has no row in v1_valuation_table.csv, so v1_verdict is null. My own reverse DCF implies the market is pricing only ~2-3% aggregate FCF growth (plus buyback-driven per-share uplift to ~3.5-4.5% per share), which is close to my own base-case per-share growth assumption (~4.5%) and to what PG is currently delivering (organic sales +1%, core EPS +1%) -- i.e. fairly priced with little cushion, implied growth roughly in line with base case, supporting INCLUDE-SMALL rather than full INCLUDE given the named growth/margin reservation. [Corrected 2026-10-08 (DV33): FY2027 guidance was already published on 29 Jul 2026 (organic +1% to +3%, core EPS in line to +3% with a $0.56 per share cost headwind, FCF productivity guided 85-90%), which triggers kill criterion 3. At Ke 7.58% (Blume beta) with SBC deducted the price implies 3.0%-3.4% aggregate growth versus roughly flat guided cash flow: implied_vs_base in_line -> above; the buyback uplift is not additive to an aggregate DCF. Verdict INCLUDE-SMALL -> WATCH.]

PLD.thesis_one_line: The world's largest warehouse landlord, raising its own growth guidance three quarters running as the industrial supply glut clears, priced for almost no growth at all.
kill_criteria: Full-year Core FFO/share guidance is cut (vs. the current $6.22-$6.30 range) at the next quarterly update.
Period-end occupancy falls below 95.0% for two consecutive quarters (currently 95.5%, trending up).
Same-store cash NOI growth decelerates below 5% YoY (currently 8.5%).
Net debt rises above $40bn without a commensurate increase in stabilized NOI.
Development stabilizations fall materially below the guided $2.25-2.75bn range for the full year.
key_adverse_facts: Net debt of approximately $34.7bn against $53.7bn of Prologis-attributable equity (net debt/equity ~65%); a full net-debt/EBITDA cross-check was not completed within the time-box.
Q2 FY26 GAAP net earnings included $291.6M of combined real-estate disposition gains (vs $57.5M a year earlier), meaning ~40% of the 85% YoY EPS jump was gain-driven, not operating.

Development pipeline is expanding (starts guidance raised to $4.5-5.5bn) at the same time as the demand recovery is still unconfirmed beyond a few quarters of data, a classic REIT-cycle risk if the recovery stalls.

SEC's bulk companyfacts API was stale (last ingested Q1 2026) at the time of research; Q2 2026 figures were pulled directly from the 10-Q's own financial-statement exhibits rather than the standard XBRL API.

Recommended offer for SEGRO plc announced 4 Aug 2026 (about GBP 14.0bn, 0.0920 PLD shares per SEGRO share, partial cash alternative up to about GBP 3.5bn via term loan, SEGRO holders 8.9%-11.5% of combined group, completion expected H1 2027) plus a 17.25M-share offering on 5-6 Aug (about $2.4bn net): dilution, leverage (kill criterion: net debt above $40bn) and integration risk not analysed in the dossier [Added 2026-10-08: DV33]
data_conflicts: The triage's claim of 'a -26% EPS print' lapping one-time gains could not be reproduced from any primary filing reviewed; every quarter checked from Q1 FY25 onward showed positive YoY EPS growth. The triage's underlying point (GAAP prints are gain-distorted) is independently corroborated even though the specific -26% figure is not.
PLD.confidence_in_thesis: medium-high (three consecutive quarterly guidance raises on Core FFO, occupancy and same-store NOI are strong, verifiable evidence; leverage and pipeline risk keep this from high confidence)
PLD.scenario_basis: Starting FY2026 Core FFO/share guidance midpoint $6.26; base case assumes FFO/share growth decelerating from 2026's high-single-digit guided pace toward ~5-6%/yr, a flat ~21.3x P/FFO, and a ~3.2% dividend yield; bear assumes growth stalls (supply glut returns, cap rates rise) and the multiple compresses to ~17x; bull assumes the current high-single-digit pace persists and the multiple expands to ~23x.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: PLD has no row in v1_valuation_table.csv, so v1_verdict is null. My own reverse DCF implies the market is pricing only ~3% long-run FFO growth, below my own base-case assumption of ~5-6%/yr and well below the high-single-to-low-double-digit Core FFO/share growth the company is currently guiding to and delivering -- i.e. cheap relative to its own near-term trajectory (implied growth below base case), with the risk that the trajectory itself is partly cyclical, which is why this is INCLUDE-SMALL rather than full INCLUDE. [Corrected 2026-10-08 (DV33): the reverse DCF used Ke 7.8%, Core FFO as cash and a $124bn equity value excluding units. On AFFO (about $5.7bn), equity $129bn and Ke 10.19% (Blume beta) the price implies 9.3% a year (7.2% at Ke 9.19%) versus a 5-6% base: above, not cheap. The dossier also omits the 4 Aug 2026 recommended all-share offer for SEGRO plc (GBP 14.0bn, up to GBP 3.5bn cash, H1 2027 completion) and the 5 Aug equity raise, and counts three guidance raises where there were two. Verdict INCLUDE-SMALL -> WATCH (provisional pending re-underwrite).]
